THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 11.03.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 MACA NO. 127 OF 2016 3 2025:KER:22093  JUDGMENT

The petitioners in O.P.(M.V.) No.1168 of 2011 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Palakkad are the appellants herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal)
2. The O.P. was filed under under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, by the parents of Master Vishnu, who died in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 31.01.2009.

According to them, on 31.01.2009 at about 4.45 p.m. while the deceased was travelling in an autorickshaw, a goods tempo van driven by the 2 nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit against the autorickshaw and as a result Vishnu sustained serious injuries and he succumbed to the injuries on the same day.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner and the 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioners, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. was Rs.3,73,000/-.

4. The insurance company filed a written statement,
admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5.
The evidence in the case consists of documentary evidence, namely Exts.A1 to A30.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioners preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioners is regarding the compensation awarded under the head loss of dependency.
He also argued that the compensation awarded under the other heads are also on the lower side.

11. On the other hand the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the 3rd respondent would argue that in the light of the decision in National Insurance Company Ltd. and others v. Assainar [2019 (4)
KLT 39], the maximum compensation that can be paid is Rs.5,00,000/-.

KLT 39]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The learned Standing Counsel also relied upon the decision in Meena Devi v. Nunu Chand Mahto @ Nemchand Mahto and Others [2023 (1) SCC 204], in which a child of 12 years died in a road accident in the year 2003 and the Hon'ble apex Court awarded a total compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-.
12.

entities.text: Meena Devi v. Nunu Chand Mahto @ Nemchand Mahto and Others [2023 (1) SCC 204]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is true that as per the decision in Assainar (Supra) the annual income provided for the year 2009-2010 is Rs.50,000/- and the multiplier to be applied is 15 and 1/3 of the income is to be MACA NO. 127 OF 2016 6 2025:KER:22093 deducted towards personal living expenses.

Therefore,
the compensation payable under the head loss of dependency will come to Rs.5,00,000/-.

However,
in the decision in Kusmi Devi vs. Md. Kasim and Others [MANU/SC/1124/2023], the Hon'ble Supreme Court has awarded a total sum of Rs.6,00,000/-.

entities.text: Kusmi Devi vs. Md. Kasim and Others [MANU/SC/1124/2023]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case a three year old child died in the accident and the accident was occurred in the year 1994.
13. In the above circumstances, I hold that, in this case also, towards non-pecuniary heads a sum of Rs.6 lakhs can be awarded as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision Kusmi Devi (supra).
14. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

15. Therefore, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.6,50,000/-,

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and the 3 rd respondent is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.6,50,000/- (Rupees Six Lakh Fifty Thousand Only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest at the rate ordered by the Tribunal from the date of the petition till realisation/deposit, within a period of two months from today.
The enhanced compensation will carry interest @8%.

On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioners, in the ratio fixed by the Tribunal, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.
